canonical.label: AGI achieved or demonstrated
canonical.definition: An AI system is publicly demonstrated or declared to match humans across most cognitive tasks; excludes narrow AI gains.

canonical.label: AI surpasses human intelligence
canonical.definition: AI clearly outperforms humans in most or all cognitive domains (superintelligence), beyond merely matching experts.

canonical.label: AI agents become routine office workers
canonical.definition: AI assistants and agents become standard tools or workers for office, software and research tasks.

canonical.label: Binding AI governance frameworks
canonical.definition: Major powers adopt international or national regulation or treaties on advanced AI.

canonical.label: Automation-driven labor and political upheaval
canonical.definition: Mass automation causes large unemployment, inequality or political instability, leading to economic redistribution or a post-work framework.

canonical.label: Robots take over physical labor
canonical.definition: Humanoid or general-purpose robots become common and cheaper than humans for most physical work.

canonical.label: Major AI-enabled attack or rogue-AI crisis
canonical.definition: An AI-enabled cyberattack, autonomous weapons conflict or near-catastrophic AI incident forces regulatory or governance action.

canonical.label: Quantum computing becomes mainstream
canonical.definition: Quantum computers are commercially deployed or in widespread use.

canonical.label: Brain-computer interfaces widely adopted
canonical.definition: Brain-computer or neural interfaces become common consumer or medical devices.

canonical.label: Human-AI merging
canonical.definition: Human cognition is merged or deeply integrated with AI, including symbiosis or fusion.

canonical.label: Mind uploading achieved
canonical.definition: Human minds are transferred or emulated in digital substrates, including whole-brain emulation.

canonical.label: Digital minds gain legal personhood
canonical.definition: Emulated or AI minds receive legal recognition or rights.

canonical.label: Digital minds outnumber biological humans
canonical.definition: Post-biological or digital intelligences exceed biological humans in number or in economic and cultural output.

canonical.label: Humanity becomes post-biological
canonical.definition: Most or all of humanity transitions to a non-biological existence; biological humans are extinct or marginal.

canonical.label: Unmodified humans become a protected minority
canonical.definition: Baseline biological humans are a small, protected group among modified or digital descendants.

canonical.label: Technological singularity
canonical.definition: An explicit singularity or transcendence event occurs; excludes ordinary AGI milestones.

canonical.label: Commercial fusion power
canonical.definition: A fusion plant connects to the grid and supplies commercial electricity, or net-power fusion is demonstrated.

canonical.label: Fusion becomes dominant energy source
canonical.definition: Fusion supplies most or a large share of global energy.

canonical.label: Renewables overtake fossil fuels
canonical.definition: Solar, wind, storage and nuclear supply most electricity or new energy investment, or surpass fossil fuels.

canonical.label: Global emissions peak
canonical.definition: Global CO2 or greenhouse gas emissions reach a peak and begin to decline.

canonical.label: Net-zero emissions reached
canonical.definition: Global or major-economy net carbon emissions reach roughly zero.

canonical.label: Warming passes 1.5°C
canonical.definition: Global temperature exceeds 1.5°C above preindustrial levels, in a single year or on a sustained basis.

canonical.label: Warming passes 2°C
canonical.definition: Global temperature exceeds 2°C above preindustrial levels.

canonical.label: Climate stabilizes at a warmer level
canonical.definition: Global temperature plateaus or begins to fall at a level above preindustrial, around 2–2.5°C.

canonical.label: Large-scale carbon removal
canonical.definition: Carbon removal or direct air capture operates at industrial scale and begins to lower atmospheric CO2.

canonical.label: Large-scale geoengineering deployed
canonical.definition: Solar or other planetary geoengineering is deployed to moderate or stabilize the climate.

canonical.label: Climate returned to near preindustrial
canonical.definition: Active restoration brings climate and atmosphere back toward preindustrial conditions.

canonical.label: Mass climate migration and refugee crisis
canonical.definition: Climate impacts force displacement of tens of millions to billions of people.

canonical.label: Climate-driven conflict and food crises
canonical.definition: Heat, water stress or crop failure triggers regional wars or global food shortages.

canonical.label: Climate tipping points crossed
canonical.definition: Major tipping points, such as ice-sheet collapse or regional climate collapse, are reached.

canonical.label: Sea-level rise forces coastal retreat
canonical.definition: Rising seas of roughly 0.5–2 m force coastal fortification, managed retreat or redrawn coastlines.

canonical.label: Multi-meter sea-level rise from ice sheets
canonical.definition: Long-term ice sheet loss raises sea levels several meters, with Greenland or Antarctica largely melting.

canonical.label: Ecosystems and biodiversity restored
canonical.definition: Rewilding, de-extinction or ecological engineering restores biodiversity and biospheres.

canonical.label: Global population peaks
canonical.definition: World population reaches its maximum, roughly 9.5–11 billion, and begins to decline.

canonical.label: Earth's population falls far below peak
canonical.definition: Earth's population declines to a few billion or less through low fertility and emigration.

canonical.label: Aging therapies extend healthy lifespan
canonical.definition: Senolytics, gene therapy or rejuvenation extend healthy life beyond 100–120 years.

canonical.label: Lifespans of 150+ years or near-immortality
canonical.definition: Lifespans reach 150 years or more, or aging is effectively conquered.

canonical.label: Hereditary diseases eliminated by gene editing
canonical.definition: Gene or cell therapies cure or eliminate hereditary and many chronic diseases, including most cancers.

canonical.label: Human germline editing becomes routine
canonical.definition: Heritable embryo editing is performed and becomes widely accepted or routine.

canonical.label: Human cloning or cryo-revival
canonical.definition: A human is cloned, revived from cryopreservation, or a historical figure is resurrected.

canonical.label: Humanity diverges into distinct lineages
canonical.definition: Humans split into distinct subspecies, clades or species through engineering or isolation, including in space.

canonical.label: Aging populations strain societies
canonical.definition: Aging and shrinking populations force changes to pensions, healthcare, migration and the economy.

canonical.label: Post-scarcity economy emerges
canonical.definition: Automation and abundant energy end material scarcity, poverty and hunger.

canonical.label: Severe pandemic or engineered pathogen
canonical.definition: A natural or engineered pandemic kills millions or tens of millions.

canonical.label: Binding global biosecurity and tech governance
canonical.definition: A crisis leads to strict global controls over existential technologies such as AI and biotech.

canonical.label: Nuclear or bioweapon catastrophe
canonical.definition: A regional nuclear war or weapons accident causes devastation or a temporary climate shock.

canonical.label: Supervolcano or VEI-7 eruption
canonical.definition: A very large eruption cools the climate and causes crop failures.

canonical.label: Asteroid or comet threat and planetary defense
canonical.definition: An asteroid or comet impact threat is deflected or narrowly missed, or an impact causes devastation.

canonical.label: Natural cosmic hazard to civilization
canonical.definition: A solar superstorm, gamma-ray burst, magnetic pole reversal or similar natural hazard disrupts civilization.

canonical.label: Civilizational collapse or dark age
canonical.definition: A major collapse, dark age or long stagnation occurs and civilization may recover.

canonical.label: Humanity's survival uncertain
canonical.definition: Forecasts state that humanity's continued existence or form is uncertain, ranging from extinction to flourishing.

canonical.label: Reusable heavy-lift rockets slash launch costs
canonical.definition: Fully reusable heavy launchers cut launch costs by an order of magnitude.

canonical.label: Humans return to the Moon
canonical.definition: Crewed landing on the Moon after Apollo.

canonical.label: Permanent lunar base established
canonical.definition: A permanently occupied or self-sustaining base is set up on the Moon.

canonical.label: Lunar city of thousands
canonical.definition: Lunar settlement grows to thousands or tens of thousands of residents.

canonical.label: First crewed Mars landing
canonical.definition: Humans first land on Mars.

canonical.label: Permanent Mars settlement founded
canonical.definition: A permanent base or colony is established on Mars.

canonical.label: Mars becomes self-sufficient
canonical.definition: Mars settlement is independent of Earth resupply for food, water and manufacturing.

canonical.label: Mars population reaches 100,000 to a million
canonical.definition: Mars population grows to six figures or more.

canonical.label: Mars terraforming
canonical.definition: Large-scale terraforming of Mars begins or advances, including a breathable atmosphere or liquid seas.

canonical.label: Asteroid mining operational
canonical.definition: Commercial asteroid mining becomes profitable and supplies metals to Earth or space.

canonical.label: Large orbital habitats built
canonical.definition: Rotating or O'Neill-type space habitats house large populations.

canonical.label: Settlements on outer-system moons and asteroid belt
canonical.definition: Humans settle the asteroid belt or moons of Jupiter and Saturn.

canonical.label: Solar system fully colonized
canonical.definition: Humans have settled across the solar system, with large off-Earth populations.

canonical.label: Earth becomes a nature or heritage preserve
canonical.definition: Earth is mainly a cultural, ecological or historical reserve.

canonical.label: Off-world settlements gain autonomy or independence
canonical.definition: Mars or other colonies declare independence or gain formal autonomy from Earth.

canonical.label: Conflict between Earth and space populations
canonical.definition: War or political crisis erupts between Earth and off-world polities or over solar-system resources.

canonical.label: Space-based solar power supplies Earth
canonical.definition: Orbital solar collectors beam substantial energy to Earth and habitats.

canonical.label: Dyson swarm construction and capture of solar output
canonical.definition: Solar collector swarms or a Dyson sphere are built and capture a significant fraction of the Sun's output.

canonical.label: Kardashev Type I reached
canonical.definition: Humanity harnesses planetary-scale energy.

canonical.label: Kardashev Type II or III reached
canonical.definition: Civilization harnesses stellar or galactic-scale energy.

canonical.label: First interstellar probe launched
canonical.definition: A robotic probe is launched toward another star, including Starshot-type or self-replicating probes.

canonical.label: Interstellar probe reaches and reports from another star
canonical.definition: A probe arrives at Proxima, Alpha Centauri or Trappist-1 and returns data.

canonical.label: Generation ship departs
canonical.definition: A crewed multi-generation ship departs for an exoplanet.

canonical.label: First human settlement in another star system
canonical.definition: Humans or post-humans establish the first permanent settlement outside the solar system.

canonical.label: Dozens of star systems settled
canonical.definition: Settlements spread to a dozen or more nearby star systems within tens of light-years.

canonical.label: Milky Way colonized
canonical.definition: Human descendants widely settle the Milky Way or form a galactic civilization.

canonical.label: Intergalactic travel or expansion
canonical.definition: Humanity or its descendants reach other galaxies, such as Andromeda or the Local Group.

canonical.label: First contact with alien intelligence
canonical.definition: Confirmed contact or signals from extraterrestrial intelligence, including its technosignatures.

canonical.label: Extraterrestrial microbial life discovered
canonical.definition: Evidence of alien microbial life is found on another world.

canonical.label: No alien civilizations found
canonical.definition: Surveys or probes find no evidence of extraterrestrial technological civilizations.

canonical.label: World government or planetary council
canonical.definition: A unified global governing authority or end of nation-states is established.

canonical.label: Institutions, languages and nations transformed beyond recognition
canonical.definition: Present-day states, languages, religions and institutions have vanished or changed unrecognizably.

canonical.label: 21st-century memory fades or is curated
canonical.definition: Historical knowledge of the present era becomes a specialist canon, maintained by long-lived institutions or AI archives.

canonical.label: Multi-star descendant civilization in year 10000
canonical.definition: By 10000, human descendants live across the solar system and nearby stars as a diverse, possibly post-human civilization.

canonical.label: Sun's aging and cosmic end-state
canonical.definition: Solar brightening or red giant expansion makes Earth uninhabitable, or the universe approaches heat death.

canonical.label: Transcendence and exotic cosmic engineering
canonical.definition: Descendants merge into a universal consciousness, or perform stellar engineering, multiverse exploration or other exotic physics.
